channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Sign 15 Cooperation Documents
item.description: Tajikistan and South Korea signed 15 new cooperation documents in Seoul on September 16, 2026. The agreements cover customs, intellectual property, education, economy, anti-corruption, financial intelligence, industry, transport, digital reforestation, export, labor safety, energy, public service, and law enforcement cooperation.

item.title: Economist Warns of Tax or Pension Age Increase to Balance System
item.description: Economist Otabek Bakirov stated that if the retirement age is not extended, taxes will need to be raised. He suggested increasing the social tax from 12% to 15% as the easiest option, but considers this approach incorrect. Alternatively, the retirement age could be increased.

item.title: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency to open office in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) plans to open a representative office in Kyrgyzstan to support Korean companies. This was announced during a meeting between South Korean National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Bilateral trade has doubled, reaching $3.4 billion in 2025.

item.title: UN reports global freshwater reserves are diminishing
item.description: The World Meteorological Organization reports that global land freshwater reserves continue to shrink while glaciers retreat, potentially leading to severe consequences for populations and economies. The report indicates that rivers worldwide experienced one of the driest periods in over three decades in 2025, with water cycles becoming more unstable.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sets fixed prices for beef and mutton to stabilize market
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's antimonopoly service has established fixed prices for beef and mutton to stabilize the market. Prices vary by region, with boneless beef ranging from 840 to 880 soms per kilogram and bone-in beef between 690 and 705 soms wholesale, and 750 to 775 soms retail. Mutton prices also differ regionally.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan presents critical minerals development strategy in Seoul
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Natural Resources, Ecology, and Technical Supervision, Akyl Toktobayev, presented the country's critical minerals development strategy at the Korea-Central Asia Business Summit in Seoul. He highlighted Kyrgyzstan's resource potential and the need to diversify the mining sector, inviting international partners for cooperation in exploration, extraction, and processing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's processing sector sees significant growth driven by beverages and bread
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's processing sector grew by 8.4% in the first eight months of 2026 compared to last year. Non-alcoholic beverage and mineral water producers led with over 20.3 billion soms, while bakeries increased output by 17.5%. Overall food processing, beverage, and tobacco production reached 81.8 billion soms.

item.title: Dushanbe to host SCO Transport and Logistics exhibition in October
item.description: An international exhibition titled "SCO Transport and Logistics" will be held in Dushanbe from October 19-20, coinciding with the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO). The event aims to showcase member states' potential in transport and logistics, foster business partnerships, and discuss seamless logistics routes within the SCO.

item.title: CSTO forces conduct 'Rubezh-2026' exercise in Kazakhstan, practicing combat scenarios
item.description: The second phase of the 'Rubezh-2026' joint exercise for the CSTO Central Asian Regional Rapid Deployment Force (CSTO CRDF) began September 16 in Kazakhstan. Servicemembers are practicing occupying a responsibility zone and eliminating simulated illegal armed groups.

item.title: Tajikistan seeks additional $1 billion for Rogun Dam construction
item.description: Tajikistan is seeking to raise an additional $1 billion to continue the construction of the Rogun Dam. The funds will be allocated for the construction of remaining facilities on the right bank of the dam.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea's SK Specialty Discuss Tungsten Project
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Industry and New Technologies met with SK Specialty in Seoul to discuss a project for an integrated tungsten value chain. The initiative aims to cover the entire process from mining to production, including the creation of a special purpose company and a centralized processing hub.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Addresses Tajikistan-South Korea Cooperation at Korea University
item.description: During an official visit, Tajik President Emomali Rahmon spoke at Korea University, expressing gratitude for an honorary doctorate. He highlighted growing bilateral ties and discussed educational reforms in Tajikistan, noting a significant increase in universities and student enrollment. Rahmon expressed interest in continued academic exchange with South Korean institutions.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korean LS MnM Sign Memorandum on Mining Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Industry and New Technologies and South Korea's LS MnM Inc. signed a memorandum of understanding to cooperate in the mining sector. The agreement focuses on attracting investment, developing mineral deposits, and enhancing deep processing of raw materials in Tajikistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan-South Korea Relations Enter New Chapter After Seoul Summit
item.description: Uzbek President's press secretary Sherzod Asadov noted that Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's visit to South Korea was marked by warm meetings and discussions. The South Korean side reportedly showed great respect and attention to the state visit of the Uzbek president.

item.title: Concerns Arise Over Textbook Sales Amid Kyrgyzstan's 12-Year Education Transition
item.description: Parents in Kyrgyzstan are complaining about a shortage of new textbooks required for the 12-year education system, forcing them to buy books independently. While officials urge against spreading unverified information and illegal purchases, law enforcement is investigating textbook sales in markets. Significant funds have been allocated for textbook printing.

item.title: SCNS Deputy Chairman Appointed Honorary President of Kyrgyzstan's Judo Federation
item.description: Akylbek Namazov, deputy chairman of Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security, has been appointed Honorary President of the National Judo Federation. Other leadership changes include the appointment of Aitmagomed Ismagombetov as First Vice-President and Emilbek Abdraliev as Vice-President. Kamil Magomedov was introduced as a new national team coach.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes program to fund rural youth university education with regional work commitment
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a program to fund university education for at least five rural youth from each district annually. Graduates must return to their region and work for a minimum of three years after obtaining their diplomas. The program aims to address regional specialist needs, prioritizing fields like medicine, education, and agriculture.

item.title: Taliban seeks Kyrgyzstan's support after joining UN Security Council
item.description: Following Kyrgyzstan's election as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council for 2027-2028, the Taliban government has requested support. The Taliban aims to leverage this position to advance its interests and strengthen political and economic ties with its neighbor.

item.title: Seven children left without parental care returned to Uzbekistan from Russia
item.description: Seven children who were left without parental care in Russia have been returned to Uzbekistan. Measures are being taken to ensure their rights and legal interests, facilitate their return to a family environment, and provide social, medical, and psychological support.

item.title: Uzbekistan Leads CIS Fixed Internet Speed Ranking
item.description: Uzbekistan improved its global Speedtest Global Index ranking in August 2026, rising three positions for both mobile and fixed internet. The country now ranks first in the CIS for fixed internet connection speed. Average mobile download speeds increased to 65.27 Mbps, and fixed speeds rose to 94.50 Mbps.

item.title: EU Pledges Winter Support for Ukraine, Calls for Air Defense
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen pledged EU support for Ukraine this winter, anticipating the toughest period since the Russian invasion. The EU plans humanitarian aid, energy supply reinforcement, and enhanced air defense. She urged immediate delivery of US Patriot systems and proposed developing a European, NATO-independent security threat response mechanism.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host Second Presidential Chess Cup
item.description: Dushanbe will host the second Presidential Chess Cup of Tajikistan from November 9 to 17, 2026. The tournament is considered a major Central Asian chess event, attracting grandmasters and young talents. The prize fund is $60,000 USD, with participants competing in two groups based on rating.

item.title: New pediatric intensive care unit opens in Samarkand region hospital
item.description: A six-bed pediatric intensive care unit has opened at the central hospital in Jambay district, Samarkand region. The Public Foundation for Civil Society Support funded the project with 3 billion Uzbek soums, acquiring 39 units of modern medical equipment. This specialized unit will improve healthcare for children in the district.

item.title: New cooperation system aims to boost incomes in Kanlykul district
item.description: Business Development Bank is implementing measures to ensure employment and increase incomes in Kanlykul district. The bank's chairman visited the district, meeting entrepreneurs and reviewing microbusiness projects. An agreement was reached to establish a training center for strawberry cultivation cooperation involving 100 households.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea elevate partnership to new level
item.description: A business forum in Seoul demonstrated a new level of strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and South Korea. President Mirziyoyev outlined economic priorities, calling for investment in new production facilities, technologies, and infrastructure. The goal is to make Uzbekistan a major regional production, technological, and export hub.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ranks First in CIS for Fixed Internet Speed, Mobile Speed Also Increases
item.description: Uzbekistan has become the leader among CIS countries in fixed internet speed. In August, download speeds increased from 62.42 Mbit/s to 65.27 Mbit/s, moving the country from 75th to 72nd globally. Mobile internet speeds also saw growth.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Increases Labor Migration Quota to 120,000 for 2027
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan has raised the quota for labor migrants entering the country to 120,000 for 2027. Previous quotas for 2025 and 2026 were also significantly increased. Countries like China, India, and Turkey are among those requesting quotas.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to remediate sites from former uranium production in Kaji-Sai
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations is preparing to remediate sites left from uranium production in Kaji-Sai village. The work includes dismantling buildings and relocating radioactive waste. Discussions are underway with Rosatom for full remediation of the area around the tailings pond.

item.title: Uzbekistan enacts new law to enhance support for victims of violence
item.description: Uzbekistan's President signed a law on September 11 to improve social services for victims of oppression and violence. The legislation aims to remove practical and administrative barriers, expand legal guarantees, and ensure victims receive qualified state-funded legal aid and social support.

item.title: Erkin Bakirov Appointed Director of Fisheries Department
item.description: Erkin Bakirov has been appointed as the director of the Department of Fisheries, as reported by the Ministry of Agriculture. Bakirov, born in 1982, holds degrees in law and finance and has previously held several responsible government positions.

item.title: Uzbek President Attends First Central Asia-Korea Business Summit in Seoul
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in the first Central Asia-Korea Business Summit in Seoul. Leaders from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan also attended. Mirziyoyev proposed building cooperation based on complementary potentials and developing industrial cooperation.

item.title: Belarus Releases 25 Political Prisoners in Exchange for Easing US Sanctions
item.description: Belarus has released 25 political prisoners following talks between President Lukashenko and US Special Representative John Koul. In return, the US will lift sanctions on two Belarusian enterprises, "Lakokraska" and "Bellesbumprom." Further releases and sanctions relief are expected as remaining issues are resolved.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Increase Retirement Age by Three Years
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning to increase the retirement age for both women and men by three years, citing an increase in the average life expectancy. The director of the Pension Fund explained the reasons behind this decision. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Bishkek Honors Soldiers Who Died Defending Kyrgyzstan's Border
item.description: An event was held in Bishkek to honor the memory of servicemen who heroically died defending the state border of Kyrgyzstan. Deputy Interior Minister Oktay Urmambetov and other officials attended. Gratitude letters were presented to soldiers who participated in border clashes.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Elevate Cooperation to Strategic Partnership Level
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea are advancing their cooperation to a new level of strategic partnership. This involves integrating technologies, finance, science, human capital, and production into a unified economic chain, focusing on industrial cooperation and high-value sectors like robotics and pharmaceuticals.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Sign Memorandum on Border Intellectual Property Protection
item.description: Tajikistan and South Korea have signed a memorandum of cooperation on protecting intellectual property rights at the border. The agreement aims to strengthen the legal framework for bilateral customs cooperation, facilitate information exchange, and enhance mutual assistance in preventing and investigating customs violations.

item.title: Tajikistan Invites Diaspora Abroad to Invest in the National Economy
item.description: Tajikistan is calling on its citizens living abroad and migrants to invest in the country's economy. The government seeks to leverage the diaspora and migrant communities to contribute to Tajikistan's development and prosperity.

item.title: Putin Orders Capture of Donbas by Year-End, Analysis Suggests Feasibility
item.description: Russian President Putin has reportedly ordered the complete capture of Donbas by the end of the year. This objective has been presented as a primary condition for ending the war in Ukraine. The article analyzes the theoretical possibilities of achieving this goal.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Interior Ministry Academy Studies Foreign Public Security Experience in China
item.description: Representatives from the Academy of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Uzbekistan visited China to study advanced foreign practices in public security. They observed digital policing, AI technologies, and drones at an exhibition in Lianyungang. Discussions were held on integrating 'smart' systems into Uzbekistan's internal affairs bodies.

item.title: Uzbekistan to introduce residency programs for specialized medical training
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement residency programs for specialized medical training, aligning with international standards. Starting in the 2026/2027 academic year, a 'Family Medicine' residency will be introduced, with full transition to residency by 2027/2028. State grants will cover tuition and provide stipends.
